title: TypeError when parsing empty config file
body:
I get `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable` when I run `mylib parse config.yaml` and the file is empty. Expected: an empty config or a clear error. Actual: stack trace.

Reproduction:
```bash
touch config.yaml
mylib parse config.yaml
```

Version: 2.3.1, Python 3.11.
author: alice

title: Add support for streaming output to the CLI
body:
It would be great if `mylib run` could stream output as it's produced rather than buffering everything until completion. My use case: long-running pipelines where I want progress visibility.

Proposed: a `--stream` flag that prints results incrementally.

title: Documentation says X but code does Y
body:
The docs at /reference/parser say that `parse()` returns `None` on invalid input, but in 2.3.1 it raises `ParseError`. Either the docs are wrong or this is a regression. I tried both and the code raises.

```python
>>> from mylib import parse
>>> parse("invalid{}{}")
Traceback...ParseError: ...
```
